uncited: Optimization and Culling refers to techniques that reduce the computational workload of object-order volume splatting by skipping or discarding primitives that do not contribute significantly to the final image.
It solves the performance bottleneck of processing large numbers of splats, particularly in real-time rendering.

It sets itself apart from its siblings by focusing on pre-rasterization filtering (size culling) and screen-space occlusion checks (early termination) rather than geometric approximation or hardware-specific pipeline optimizations.
**Transformation:** Primitives are transformed from volume space to screen space using the Model-View-Projection (MVP) matrix or specific factorizations (e.g., shear-warp) [S2, S3, S4, unofficial].
For perspective projections, the kernel shape may be distorted (e.g., EWA splatting) to account for foreshortening [S6, unofficial][S10, unofficial].
Splatting compositing is performed along sheets (all pixels at once for a set of voxels), whereas ray-casting composites along rays (one sample at a time) [S10, unofficial].
This allows the renderer to quickly check flags before loading an order of magnitude more of additional splat data.
Early Splat Termination was introduced as an optimization for object-order volume splatting to handle occlusion efficiently in screen space [S2, unofficial][S3].
